user.title: HESC v4
user.description: Install HESC v4? Then open "HESC v4" in the sidebar: the first start asks how you charge at home and looks for your charger, car and sources. HESC v4 starts in shadow mode: it watches and switches nothing.

from_v3.title: Take over from HESC v3
from_v3.description: HESC v3 is installed. HESC v4 can start with its settings: sources, charger, car, plans and history. HESC v3 is only read and keeps running unchanged. HESC v4 starts in shadow mode: it switches nothing.

data.use_hpvc_sources: PV and grid power from HPVC

data_description.use_hpvc_sources: Use the PV and grid sensors chosen in HPVC, when HPVC has them (as in v2). Your own choice below is used otherwise.
data_description.pv_power_sensor: W or kW; kW is converted. Not needed when HPVC provides it.
data_description.grid_export_positive: Switch on when your grid sensor shows export as a positive value.
data_description.forecast_attribute: Attribute to read instead of the state; empty = use the state.
data_description.solar_today_sensor: Optional. Solcast (detailedForecast attribute) or Open-Meteo Solar Forecast (watts attribute).
data_description.irradiance_sensor: W/m², or a lux meter (lx is converted, about 120 lx per W/m²); needed when the weather station is used.
data_description.forecast_now_sensor: Optional. Leave empty when you have no solar forecast: HESC then plans on prices and charges on measured sun.
data_description.grid_power_l1_sensor: Optional, for the phase advice: the grid power of each phase from your meter (W or kW, net). HESC works out the sign itself.

data_description.ev_power_sensor: W or kW; kW is converted.
data_description.ev_soc_sensor: Recommended. Used for the charge goal, the minimum charge and 'car full'. Without it HESC plans in kWh only.

data_description.charger_eco_values: Comma separated mode values that mean the charger is in its solar mode.

no_solar_forecast.title: HESC works without a solar forecast
no_solar_forecast.description:
HESC now plans grid charging on prices only and charges on the sun it measures (PV power, or your irradiance / lux sensor). The charge plan counts no sun, so it never charges too late, and the kickstart is off.

With a solar forecast HESC plans smarter. Install one of these and choose its sensors in HESC's setup (Settings → Devices & services → HESC → Configure → Sources):
- **Solcast PV Forecast** (HACS, recommended): forecast now, in 30 minutes and today.
- **Open-Meteo Solar Forecast** (HACS): turn on its sensor "power production next 30 minutes".
- **Forecast.Solar** (built in): HESC reads its forecast series itself.

This note disappears once a forecast is chosen.

dashboard_url_taken.title: HESC dashboard not added: {url} is already in use
dashboard_url_taken.description:
HESC brings its own dashboard (sidebar: **HESC**, address {url}). Another dashboard already uses that address, probably one you made yourself by pasting HESC's YAML. HESC leaves that dashboard alone.

To use the dashboard that comes with HESC (it is updated together with HESC): delete your own dashboard under Settings → Dashboards, then reload HESC (Settings → Devices & services → HESC v3 → ⋮ → Reload) or restart Home Assistant. If the address comes from configuration.yaml or another integration, free it there.

To keep your own dashboard: ignore this notice.
